articles.title: Haryana Govt Issues 100 MWp Rooftop Solar Tender With Seven-Yrs Maintenance
articles.description: Haryana government has issued a tender for the tentative development of 100 MWp of grid-connected rooftop (GCRT) solar plants without battery banks. The bidder design, supply, erect, test and commission rooftop solar projects. The developer will also be required to provide comprehensive maintenance for seven years at various locations across Haryana and Chandigarh. It has sought bids till October 30, 2026 The scope of the rooftop solar project includes the supply of solar generation meters and bidirectional meters. The goods supplied under the contract must be fully insured by the supplier, at its own cost, against any loss or damage arising during manufacture or acquisition, transportation and delivery to the site. Once the materials have been delivered to the user site, the user department or organisation may provide a storage facility, with a lock-and-key arrangement for the supplier, for a maximum of 15 days. This provision is based on the assumption that the systems will be installed within 15 days of delivery. Generating Solar Power, Adding Meter & Bidirectional Meter The bidder is expected to add solar generation meter and bidirectional meter, along with current transformers (CTs) and potential transformers (PTs), where required and add a surge protection device (SPD). The developer also must comply with the latest specifications and accuracy classes prescribed under the applicable Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) and DISCOM instructions at the time of installation. The bidder must supply components such as wires, cables, switches, circuit breakers, connectors, junction boxes, changeover switches and other associated components the scope of the work. It would aleo be required to meet the latest applicable International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standards. Scope of Work The size and weight of the packing cases must take into consideration, where appropriate, the remoteness of the goods' final destination and the absence of heavy handling facilities at any point during transit. The scope of work also includes performance testing of the complete project, after-sales service through service centres, and coverage of the risk liability of all personnel associated with the project's implementation and execution. Following commissioning, the successful bidder must train at least one person nominated by the user at each location on various aspects of the project's design and maintenance. The successful bidder must maintain sufficient inventories of spare parts to ensure that the project remains functional throughout the warranty period. The bidder must also operate the project on a trial basis and closely monitor its performance before handing it over.
